passages.title: How Tea Is Made
passages.body: Tea is one of the most popular drinks in the world, and China is known for it. But do you know how tea is made? First, the tea leaves are picked by hand from the tea plants. This is usually done in spring, when the leaves are fresh and green. Then the leaves are dried in the sun or by machines. After that, they are processed carefully to bring out the flavor. Finally, the tea is packed and sent to shops all over the world. The whole process needs great care. Good tea is not made in a day. Next time you drink a cup of tea, remember the hard work behind it.

passages.title: The Art of Paper Cutting
passages.body: Paper cutting is a traditional Chinese art with a long history. It is loved by many people around the world. In this art, beautiful pictures are cut from paper with scissors or a knife. The pictures are often about animals, flowers, or happy events. During the Spring Festival, paper cuttings are put on windows and doors. They are believed to bring good luck. Most paper cuttings are made by hand, and each one takes a lot of time and skill. Today, this old art is still taught in many schools, so that it will not be lost. Paper cutting shows the beauty of Chinese culture.

passages.title: Clay Figures of Tianjin
passages.body: In the city of Tianjin, there is a famous traditional art called clay figures. These small figures are made of clay and are known for their lively colors and shapes. The art was started over a hundred years ago by a man named Zhang. First, soft clay is taken and shaped into people or animals by hand. Then the figures are dried and heated to make them hard. After that, they are painted in bright colors. Each figure takes several days to complete. Visitors to Tianjin often buy these figures as gifts. The clay figures are not just toys; they tell stories of Chinese life and history.

passages.title: Made in Many Countries
passages.body: Today, the things we use every day are made in many different countries. Your phone may be made in Korea, your watch in Switzerland, and your shoes in China. Why are products made all over the world? One reason is cost. Some countries can produce things at a lower price. Another reason is skill. Some places are known for special products, like cars from Germany. When you buy something, look at the label. It often tells you where the product was made. No matter where things are made, what matters most is good quality. A good product is welcomed everywhere in the world.

passages.title: A School Science Fair
passages.body: Last week, an international science fair was held at our school. Students brought many amazing things that were made by themselves. Marcus made a model plane. It was made of used wood and glass, so it was good for the environment. When people asked how it was produced, he said every part was cut and joined by hand. Anna showed a small house that was built from old boxes. My project was a kite that was painted with lively colors. The teachers said our projects were creative because they were made from everyday materials. The science fair taught us that useful things can be made from things we already have.

passages.title: Buying Local Products
passages.body: GREEN MARKET — SUPPORT LOCAL! Welcome to our Green Market! Here all the products are made by local people. FOOD: Fresh fruit and vegetables are grown on nearby farms. No long travel is needed, so they are always fresh. CRAFTS: Beautiful handbags and gloves are made by hand from local cotton. Each one is special. TOYS: Wooden toys are made from trees grown in our area. They are safe for children. WHY BUY LOCAL? Local products are fresh, and buying them helps people in our town. When you buy local, you also help protect the environment, because less traffic is needed to bring goods from far away. Come and support local products today!
